    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — unhedged FX exposure, Fed hike next week, oil at $100
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — 3-to-5-year deposit tenor interest payment risk

Synopsis:
    Indian banks, primarily state-run and private domestic lenders, have left a significant portion of their FX interest-payment obligations on ~$127B in overseas deposits unhedged. While the RBI's swap facility covers principal, interest payments remain exposed. Banks cite high hedging costs (~3%/year) and RBI intervention-supported rupee stability as justification for inaction. The risk is asymmetric: if the rupee weakens materially (toward 96–97/USD), a rush for spot dollar purchases could amplify depreciation pressure. Near-term catalysts include Brent crude approaching $100/bbl and a ~60% market-implied probability of a Fed rate hike.
